english: A shepherd, Man-Minded, was dwelling in a village. He was guarding many sheep in the field. At night sleep seized him near the enclosure. Then he saw a dream. In sleep a great wolf came forth from the hill. It seized the ram and was carrying it away. Then Man-Minded woke up, trembling. He looked at the sheep; they were lying in the enclosure. He said: "Why am I afraid? The dream has deceived me." But he did not lie down; through the night he was sleepless. Early the wolf did arrive. But the shepherd was awake, and with the dogs he drove it away. So the dream rescued the ram. And he cherished the sheep, and he did not fear the night.

english: The wife of a warrior was seeing a dream at night. A snake was lying in her own house. She became afraid, and she went to her who knows. She said: "Mother, in my sleep I saw a snake in my house. What does the dream say?" The Kindly One pointed it out: "Do not be afraid, daughter. The snake is the guardian of the household. A son will be born to you, and it will protect him." And he was born to her. The snake lay near the fire, and he grew up and was healthy. The wife gave the Kindly One a measure of flour.

english: A warrior was lying by the fire. He trembled in fear; the hostile ones were many. Then sleep came upon him, and Perkʷunos stood over him in a dream. He was grasping a pointed tool in his hand. He spoke: "Warrior, why are you afraid? I slew the serpent; I shall protect you. Early stand up, and you will overpower them." He woke up, and he did not tremble. His heart grew strong. At dawn he stood up and overpowered the hostile ones. Great fame reached him, and he praised Perkʷunos.

english: Of-Good-Horses went to the pasture and lay down under a hazel. A great sleep seized him. He lay in sleep through many nights. The leaves fell, and the leaves grew again. Then he woke up and went home. In the house a man was standing. Of-Good-Horses did not know him, and he said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am the son of Of-Good-Horses. My father went away and vanished." Then he was astonished, and he said: "Son, I am your father!" He became joyful, and he seated him by the fire. He said: "You are grown, and I was in sleep."

english: A wife was in sleep. In the night she heard someone. She woke up and caught sight of a stranger sitting by the fire. She trembled and said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am hungry and thirsty." She gave him fish and honey, and he ate and drank. Then he said: "Wife, you are good. May the gods give you good things." She lay down again, and sleep took her. Early he vanished. english: A mother laid her daughter on the ground, and sleep held her. And she was lying near her. In the night a snake was creeping toward her. But a hedgehog was awake, and it caught sight of it. She placed honey near it.

english: Of-Good-Fame was making ready a boat. At night he was seeing in a dream the boat sinking. He went to Of-Good-Mind and told her. She said: "Do not go on the water! It will swallow the boat." They brought her a gift.

english: Of-Goodly-Fame was going through the night, and he became cold. He caught sight of a fire, and near it he saw a house. Of-Good-Gifts came forth from it and said: "Guest, enter, and sit down here!" She clothed him with wool, and she gave him honey; he ate and became warm. Then she laid him down, and he was in sleep. Early he woke up: he was lying on a hill. The house had vanished, and the fire had become cold. But his heart was warm, and he was not hungry. He said: "Was this a dream, or the house of a god?" Then he was going on the way.

english: A father and his son, Of-Good-Race, were guarding the horses at night. He said: "Son, I have become tired. Watch them; I shall lie down." Of-Good-Race said: "Lie down, father; I am alert." The father was lying down in sleep; Of-Good-Race sat and looked at the horses. But sleep was creeping toward him. He stood up and walked around the horses, and he sang. At dawn he woke up: "Of-Good-Race, did you sleep?" "I did not sleep; I walked and I sang, and the horses are here." And he cherished him.
